newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's bond yields close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's bond yields close slightly higher.

text.p: Key bond yields closed slightly higher on Friday on profit taking and increased new issuances, dealers said.
Overnight call rates remained unchanged as cash liquidity continued to be abundant, they said.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.16 pct vs Thursday's 12.15
* 3-mth CDs end at 13.92 pct vs Thursday's 13.76
* Overnight call average unchanged at 13.00 pct

Three-month CD yields rose after commercial banks increased issuances to capitalise on the relatively low level of the yields, the dealers said. The yields have fallen from a year high of 15.80 percent at the end of August.
"Many banks wanted to secure funds while the CD yields were at low levels," a Hyundai Securities dealer.
The overnight call rates showed little changes as the cash liquidity remained high due to slow cash demand.
The average call rate was 13.00 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
